title: Existence of a directed Euler tour
statement: Let $D$ be a digraph on a finite, nonempty vertex set $V$ whose underlying undirected graph is connected. Then $D$ admits a directed Euler tour—a closed directed trail that traverses every arc of $D$ exactly once—if and only if every vertex $v \in V$ is balanced, meaning its outdegree and indegree agree, $d^{+}(v) = d^{-}(v)$.
hypotheses_covered: conclusion: existence of a directed Euler tour is equivalent to d^+(v) = d^-(v) for every vertex v
replaced:
\emph{\texttt{D} contains a directed Euler tour if and only if \texttt{D} is
connected and \texttt{d$^{+}$(v) = d$^{-}$(v)} for all \texttt{v $\in$ V}.}
